what_its_for: Dasiglucagon is used to treat severe low blood sugar (called severe hypoglycemia) in adults and children 6 years of age and older who have diabetes. It is a glucagon medicine that works by telling your liver to release sugar into your blood to raise your blood sugar level quickly during a dangerous low blood sugar emergency.
how_to_take: Dasiglucagon is given as a shot (injection) under the skin (subcutaneous injection). It comes as a prefilled autoinjector pen or a prefilled syringe. It is meant to be used by a caregiver, family member, or friend when you are having a severe low blood sugar episode and cannot help yourself. The injection is given in the outer thigh, upper arm, or belly (abdomen). After giving the injection, the caregiver should call emergency services (911) right away and turn you onto your side to prevent choking. When you wake up and are able to swallow safely, eat a fast-acting sugar (like juice or glucose tablets) followed by a snack or meal.
dosing: Adults and children weighing 55 pounds (25 kg) or more: One full dose of 0.6 mg (one entire autoinjector pen or prefilled syringe). Children weighing less than 55 pounds (25 kg): One half dose of 0.3 mg. Only one dose is typically needed. If the person does not wake up within 15 minutes, emergency medical help must be called immediately. Do NOT give a second dose unless directed by a healthcare provider.
missed_dose: Dasiglucagon is only used in emergencies, so there is no regular daily dosing schedule to follow. It is not taken on a routine basis. Make sure you always have your dasiglucagon kit with you or nearby in case of a severe low blood sugar emergency. Replace it before the expiration date so it is always ready to use.
storage: Store dasiglucagon in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do NOT freeze it. If needed, you may store it at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C) for up to 12 months, but do not use it past the expiration date printed on the label. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Do NOT use it if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it. Keep it in its original case until you are ready to use it. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid storing dasiglucagon in the freezer or in very hot places like a car glove compartment on a hot day. Do not use an expired kit. After using the autoinjector or syringe, do not try to reuse it. People who have a tumor of the adrenal glands (pheochromocytoma) or a tumor that releases glucagon (glucagonoma) should not use dasiglucagon. Talk to your doctor if you are unsure whether this medicine is right for you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call 911 (emergency services) immediately after giving the injection if the person does not respond or wake up within 15 minutes. Contact your doctor after every episode of severe low blood sugar, even if the person recovered well, so your diabetes treatment plan can be reviewed. Call your doctor if you notice signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you experience nausea or vomiting after using dasiglucagon, as this can be a common side effect.
when_it_works: Dasiglucagon usually starts to raise blood sugar within 10 to 15 minutes after the injection. Most people begin to wake up or become more alert within 15 minutes. If there is no response within 15 minutes, emergency medical help must be called right away. Once you are awake and able to swallow, eating a carbohydrate-containing snack or meal will help keep your blood sugar stable.
special_populations: Children: Dasiglucagon is approved for children 6 years and older. The dose is based on the child's weight. It has not been studied in children under 6 years of age. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using dasiglucagon. Severe low blood sugar is dangerous during pregnancy, and treatment is important, but your doctor can help weigh the risks and benefits. Older adults: Dasiglucagon can be used in older adults, but they may be at higher risk for low blood sugar complications. Caregivers should make sure to call for emergency help right away. Liver or kidney problems: Talk to your doctor if you have liver disease, as dasiglucagon works by stimulating the liver to release stored sugar. If your liver does not have enough stored sugar (for example, due to starvation or liver disease), dasiglucagon may not work as well.
